learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will deepen their understanding of adverbs, identify their specific types including frequency, degree, and relative adverbs, and master their correct placement in sentences.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 You already know that adverbs describe how an action happens. But did you know they also tell us how OFTEN, to what DEGREE, and exactly WHY something happened? Let's unlock the advanced power of these action-modifying words!

lesson_modules.module_title: 📊 Adverbs of Frequency and Degree (आवृत्ति और परिमाणवाचक)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Adverbs of Frequency tell us 'how often' an action happens (always, sometimes, rarely). Adverbs of Degree tell us the intensity or 'how much' of an action or quality (very, completely, almost).
examples_or_templates: Degree: I have **almost** finished my project.

lesson_modules.module_title: ❓ Interrogative and Relative Adverbs (प्रश्नवाचक और संबंधवाचक)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Interrogative adverbs are used to ask questions about time, place, manner, or reason (when, where, how, why). Relative adverbs refer back to a noun mentioned earlier and join two clauses together.
examples_or_templates: Relative: This is the house **where** I was born.
Relative: I remember the day **when** we first met.

lesson_modules.module_title: 📍 The Position of Adverbs (क्रिया विशेषण का स्थान)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Where you put the adverb matters! Adverbs of Manner usually go at the end. Adverbs of Frequency usually go BEFORE the main verb but AFTER helping verbs (like is/are).
examples_or_templates: Manner: She sang the song **beautifully**. (End of sentence)
Frequency: He **always** arrives early. (Before main verb)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the Adverb of Degree in this sentence: 'The concert was absolutely fantastic.'
❓ Which sentence shows the correct placement of the adverb 'never'?
options: I never have seen that movie.
I have seen never that movie.
I have never seen that movie.
Never I have seen that movie.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: I have never seen that movie.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a Relative Adverb: 'Tell me the reason _____ you were absent yesterday.'
subjective_practice.hint: What question word asks for a reason?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the Adverb of Frequency: 'My grandfather occasionally visits us during the holidays.'
subjective_practice.hint: Look for the word that tells you 'how often' the visits happen.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this sentence by placing the adverb in brackets in the correct position: 'I eat breakfast at 8 AM.' (usually)
subjective_practice.hint: Adverbs of frequency usually go right before the main verb.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🕵️ The Action Observer
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Watch a family member doing a chore or activity (like cooking or cleaning) for 5 minutes. Write down 5 sentences describing what they did using different types of adverbs (Manner, Time, Place, Frequency, and Degree). Label the adverbs you used!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Adverbs of Frequency (often, never) tell how often; Adverbs of Degree (very, too) tell how much.
⭐ Interrogative adverbs ask questions (why, when), and Relative adverbs join clauses (where, when).
⭐ The position of an adverb changes based on its type; frequency adverbs usually sit before the main verb.
